newsitem.title: USA: US auto makers chief says 100 yen/dlr appropriate.
newsitem.headline: US auto makers chief says 100 yen/dlr appropriate.

text.p: Automobile Manufacturers Association of America President Andrew Card said Friday U.S. officials should not "talk up" the value of the dollar, which he said ought to be around 100 yen to the dollar.
"We think the appropriate yen/dollar relationship is more in the hundred yen per dollar range," Card said in an interview with Reuters Financial television.
Card said he was pleased by comments this week by Eisuke Sakakibara, director-general of international finance at the Ministry of Finance, that suggested he saw no need to further weaken the yen.
The dollar fell against the yen on those comments and Card said he saw no reason for the U.S. government to try to turn that around when there is no currency crisis.
"We don't see any need for our government to talk up the dollar," Card said. "We hope that they will encourage the Japanese government not to talk down the yen."

The U.S. automobile manufacturers have been vocal about their concerns that Japan has been pursuing a weak yen policy, which could undermine U.S. auto sales in Japan and give Japanese manufacturers unfair pricing advantage in the United States.
